input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere (a full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing; the document is a single body section ending with General Provisions at p0063-p0073). Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per its warranty at p0035, collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor data, so it is a hosting/services vendor that processes Customer data. No insurance for such a vendor is walk-away territory under the rule, so this is a missing-clause deviation. We inserted a new General Provisions subsection (j) at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request), noting the USD 1M E&O / USD 2M cyber fallback if Kubient pushes back.

ops.text: (j) Insurance. Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: (i) commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; (ii) professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; (iii) cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000 covering Kubient's collection, processing and storage of data hereunder; and (iv) workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law. Kubient shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon request.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a standard insurance covenant, as Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and collects and stores visitor data on our behalf but the Agreement carries no insurance requirement. Our playbook position is CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M with certificates on request; we can work with E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M if needed.
proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant in General Provisions
